D3_quotes.locator: Fuls 2013, s.2 'Methods of Sign Analysis' (held cleaned text lines 163-179; journal pp. 255-256)
D3_quotes.quote: It is well known that some signs like sign 740 are mostly located in the terminal position of texts, while others are very often in initial position of texts. The preferred sign positions gives us some clues about the possible sign function assuming a language with a fixed syntax. ... The distribution of a sign position can be used to evaluate possible sign functions. B. Wells classifies some signs according to their preferred text position as Initial signs (INS), Terminal Marker (TMK), and Post-Terminal Marker (PTM). He also discovered, that sign 60 appears only in position 1 to 4 (except 5 two-lined texts), which is often replaced by sign 1 or sign 2. They are called Initial Cluster Terminal Marker (ICTM).

limb_1_class_definition.evidence: D3 (D3-Q1, D3-Q2): Wells classifies signs 'according to their preferred text position', and the ICTM class is the signs that 'mark the end of initial clusters' - a definition by cluster-final behaviour, drawn from positional distribution. D4 (D4-Q1): the ICTM is defined by its role terminating an initial cluster. D4-Q2's suggestion that ICTMs may be grammatical elements is a hypothesis about what the class might mean, offered for a class already delimited positionally; it is not a stated definition of the class and not a basis of any assignment, and under DD-043-10 it cannot be counted as one.
limb_1_class_definition.requirement: the produced documents state what ITM is, and the stated definition is not a positional one

limb_2_per_sign_basis.evidence: every basis the produced documents state is positional (terminal-position distribution for W740; initial-position / initial-cluster distribution for W820, W817, W861), and for W231 (P056) the produced documents state no basis at all - silence, which the frozen standard fixes as failure. Per-sign record in per_sign_basis.
limb_2_per_sign_basis.requirement: for each of the four ITM signs, the produced documents state a position-independent basis

limb_3_source_agreement.evidence: D4-Q1: the published ICTM class has exactly three members - signs 060, 001, 002 - none of them a builder ITM key. D3-Q3 and D4-Q3 assign 817, 820, 861 as initial signs; D4-Q5 assigns 820 as a terminal marker; D3-Q1/Q4 and D4 assign 740 terminally. W231 is omitted by both documents where the table asserts ITM. The published lists therefore assign different functions to the four signs, and omit the fourth - a gate failure under the limb's own wording.
limb_3_source_agreement.requirement: where the produced published documents list per-sign function assignments, they agree with the builder table for all four ITM signs
